## HDFC Bank ($HDFCBANK) — India's Largest Private Sector Bank

**Price: ₹746.85** (+1.15% today) | MCap: ₹11.5L Cr | **52w Range: ₹727–₹1,021**

### Key Metrics
| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| **P/E (TTM)** | **16.7×** — historically reasonable for a bank of this calibre |
| **Forward P/E** | **11.9×** — priced for ~40% earnings growth |
| **P/B** | **1.96×** — well below the 3-4× it traded pre-2023 |
| **ROE** | **13.8%** — solid, though subdued vs its 15-18% historical range |
| **Profit Margin** | **26.8%** — best-in-class for Indian private banks |
| **Dividend Yield** | **1.74%** |
| **Beta** | **0.43** — defensive; moves less than the market |

### The Story

HDFC Bank is India's largest private sector bank by assets and market cap, formed after the landmark **HDFC Ltd. merger in July 2023**.[1][8] It services the full spectrum — wholesale, retail, cards, payments, and wealth — with an unmatched branch network.

### Valuation Note

The stock has had a rough 12 months (**-23% from its 52w high** of ₹1,021). The post-merger integration, NIM compression from the rate cycle, and the recent **RBI watchlist-driven provisions** have weighed on sentiment. But at **16.7× TTM earnings and just 1.96× book**, it's the cheapest it has been in years — the forward P/E of **11.9×** leaves room if earnings ramp up.

### What to Watch
- **NIM trajectory** — merger cost synergies flow through
- **Loan growth** — India's credit cycle
- **Provisions** — any RBI regulatory overhang
- The stock is **₹20 off its 52w low** — potential double-bottom setup on the chart
